blocks.h2: Scoping the Sewer Before You Buy a Two-Flat
blocks.body: A two-flat's sewer line carries waste from two households, sometimes three, and on an older building it may be original clay. That makes it one of the biggest unknowns in the purchase. A camera inspection during your contract period shows whether the line is clean, needs regular rodding or needs a repair. You'll get the footage to share with your agent and attorney, which can make a real difference in negotiations.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a Sewer Inspection
blocks.body: Access matters most. A basement cleanout is simplest. A blocked line needs clearing first. Going through a toilet or vent takes more time. We quote a flat price before we start.

blocks.h2: Sewer Camera Questions From Ravenswood Homeowners

items.q: Should I scope the sewer before buying a two-flat?
items.answer: Yes. A standard inspection doesn't cover it, and a repair under an old building can be significant.

items.q: Can the camera see under the basement slab?
items.answer: Yes, from the cleanout all the way to the city sewer.

items.q: Can you tell if it's the city's problem?
items.answer: Yes. We follow the line to the main and show you where the problem is.
Yes, to share with a seller, an agent or other owners.

items.q: Will you inspect under-slab drains too?
items.answer: If we can reach them from a floor drain or cleanout, yes.

items.q: Can you inspect a line with no cleanout?
items.preview: Usually, through a toilet or vent.
items.answer: Usually. We can go through a toilet flange or roof vent if needed.

items.q: How much does a sewer camera inspection cost in Ravenswood?
items.preview: It depends on access and length. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on access and the length of the line. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
